architecture.approach: Keep the existing JwtStrategy/TenantContext scope resolution and make it reusable and complete: add scoped-filter helpers to TenancyService, refactor the hand-written invitation and membership filters onto them, scope audit writes and reads from TenantContext, and fix the refresh-token scope defect by adding a nullable clinicId that carries the selected workspace across rotation. No dependency and no permission-matrix work (BP-011) are added.

components.name: TenancyService
components.description: Adds clinicFilter(), organizationFilter() and assertClinicInScope(), and refactors the existing tenant predicates onto them.

components.name: OnboardingService
components.description: Uses the shared helper for the pending-invitation list instead of a hand-written clinic filter.

components.name: AuditService
components.description: Defaults organizationId/clinicId from TenantContext on write and tenant-scopes listForEntity.

components.name: auth.service
components.description: Persists the active clinic when issuing and switching refresh tokens, and keeps that scope on refresh; fixes the D5 fallback.

components.name: InviteDto
components.description: Documents clinicId as a selector that is re-verified inside the caller's organization.

components.name: SwitchWorkspaceDto
components.description: Documents clinicId as a selector that is re-verified against the caller's memberships.

components.name: JwtStrategy
components.description: Existing scope resolution and active-membership check; unchanged.

dataModel.flowDescription: Login issues a refresh token carrying the active scope's clinicId; a workspace switch re-issues it with the selected clinic; refresh resolves that membership, rejects an inactive one, and rotates with the same clinic. Legacy rows with clinicId null fall back to the default scope once, then carry the scope.

securityConsiderations.description: Tenant scope is resolved only from the verified token and the active membership; no request body, query or header value can widen it. Navigation hiding is not a security boundary.
The global ValidationPipe rejects undeclared body fields, and the two selector DTOs re-verify their clinicId against the caller's memberships.
All access goes through Prisma's parameterised client; no raw SQL is introduced.

dependencies.name: @prisma/client
dependencies.notes: Parameterised queries only; one additive migration adds refresh_tokens.clinicId.

dependencies.name: class-validator
dependencies.notes: Existing DTO validation, including the selector fields.

risks.description: A future service could bypass the helper and hand-write a weaker filter.
risks.mitigation: Documented rule, refactor of every current filter, and cross-tenant tests enumerating clinic-scoped endpoints.

risks.description: Patient isolation cannot be tested until BP-015 exists.
risks.mitigation: The helper and rule ship here; BP-015 must add the patient-resource test.

risks.description: Returning 403 for a foreign id discloses existence.
Organization-wide roles must not be narrowed by accident.
risks.mitigation: The helper takes the verified scope including the organization-wide case.

risks.description: Legacy refresh tokens predate the clinicId column.
risks.mitigation: Nullable column and a one-rotation default fallback before the scope is carried.
